speakeroldname: Hon. G. H. BOIVLN (Minister of Customs and Excise):
speakerposition: Minister of Customs and Excise
subsubtopic: MOTION FOR THE PRODUCTION OF INSPECTOR DUNCAN'S REPORT
speechtext:
When this resolution was submitted to the House on March 15 last I asked that it be transferred from the order

Customs Inquiry
"Notices of Motions for the Production of Papers" to the order 'Notices of Motions,'not because I desired to debate it at any length but because I felt it my duty to explain to the House why, in my humble opinion, this report should not be laid upon the table at the present time. If the motion carries, the government will be requested to lay upon the table a copy of the report made by Inspector Walter Duncan concerning the administration of the customs service at the port of Montreal, during the month of December, 1925, together with evidence and other documents. It is absolutely impossible for the government to comply with that order if it is made, because the government has not in its possession the original report. The original report has already been produced by the Minister of Customs and Excise, to whom it was made, before the committee which is now investigating the administration of the Department of Customs. The report is no longer in the possession of the government. It has already been handed over to a committee of the House. The members of that committee have had access not only to the interim report but to the complete report prepared when the investigation at Montreal was completed. They have also had access to all the evidence taken by Inspector Duncan in the course of his investigation into the affairs of the port of Montreal. The report made to the minister was a confidential report made by one of the employees of the government who was sent to Montreal on a confidential mission to ascertain how the officers of the department were conducting its affairs, and whether or not any of them were guilty of graft, corruption, dishonesty, or irregularity of any kind.
Now, may I explain to the House how the investigation in question was held? Inspector Duncan made an ex parte inquiry. He caused to be brought before him, either at the customs office at Montreal or in a room at the Windsor hotel, not only the officers of the Department of Customs-and I say at once that if any of those officers were proved dishonest I do not want to shield them-but also several other persons who had had dealings with the departmental officers at the port. All these people, whether they were accused or not came before Inspector Duncan and were examined. They were examined without being represented by counsel, they were not allowed to offer any defence in their own behalf. I respectfully represent to hon. gentlemen that it would be unfair to these persons to have this report tabled with the evidence upon which it was based,
in view of the fact that they had no opportunity of defending themselves or of summoning witnesses in their own behalf.
If these reasons are not sufficient to justify the House in refusing to order the production of a confidential report there is the added reason that this document has already been produced. It has been before a committee of this House for at least six weeks, and every member of that committee has had access to it. I am sure that there are members of the committee now in the House who will bear me out in the statement that there are certain conclusions in that report which have not been taken up by the committee and which the committee has decided not to publish at the present time. By unanimous consent the report was produced and not filed before the committee.
Let me give another reason why a copy of the report should not be tabled. The House has appointed a committee to judge these same customs officers and officials upon the evidence now being adduced before the committee. It was appointed to make a report to this House, to give the House the names of the different officers who were unworthy of retaining their positions, the names of the different officers, who perhaps should be prosecuted for illegalities or irregularities in the performance of their duty. The committee must also establish responsibility, determine to what extent the officers themselves are responsible for these irregularities, and to what extent these irregularities were condoned or approved by the minister and by the higher officers in the department in Ottawa.
I ask you, Mr. Speaker, and I ask the House, are we going to be prejudiced, is the public of *Canada going to be prejudiced by reading and by having produced as official, the conclusions drawn by Inspector Duncan? I have nothing to say against Inspector Duncan. I chose Inspector Duncan to make the investigation because he was highly recommended by the Minister of Finance and because he had the reputation of being an honest and efficient official of the Department of Finance. I was glad to send him to Montreal. He did his duty. In so far as he had time to do it, I think he did it well. Without saying a word against Inspector Duncan, I contend that the House does not desire to be influenced by his personal opinion but would prefer to rely upon the judgment of the committee appointed to investigate these matters, to pass upon them and to make a report. What advantage can there be, except possibly some petty political advantage in making public the contents of this report while the same
Questions

matters are under investigation? If hon. members who take part in this debate when it is resumed, are in a position to explain any advantage to the House in having the report tabled at present, if the right hon. leader of the opposition (Mr. Meighen) or any other hon. member can explain how the government can prepare a copy of the report and comply with the order of the House, when the report is not in the possession of the government, I should like them to do so. An order was made by the committee calling upon the^ Minister of Customs to submit the confidential report received from Inspector Duncan to the committee and make it available to the members of the committee. I was glad to comply with that request. I no longer have the report.
